title: Cost-Based Query Planning & Statistics
description: Understand cost constants (seq_page_cost, random_page_cost), histogram statistics in pg_statistic, and planner hints.

data.text: PostgreSQL uses a **Cost-Based Optimizer (CBO)**. The planner evaluates multiple query execution paths (various index scans, join orders, sort methods) and selects the path with the lowest calculated cost units.

By default, PostgreSQL sets `random_page_cost = 4.0` and `seq_page_cost = 1.0`, modeling spinning hard drives where seeking is 4x slower. On modern NVMe SSDs, random seeks are virtually as fast as sequential reads! Lowering `random_page_cost` encourages the planner to use indexes instead of sequential scans.

data.title: Tuning Cost Constants for NVMe SSD Storage
data.content: postgresql.conf optimization for modern cloud drives.

data.text: Using Statistics to Change the Plan

The planner estimates row counts from statistics collected by `ANALYZE`. If the estimate is far from reality, the chosen plan can be wrong. Raising the statistics target on a column with skewed data, or forcing a fresh `ANALYZE` after a bulk load, is often enough to fix a bad plan without touching the query.

data.title: Raise statistics granularity and re-check the plan
data.content: A higher target builds a more detailed histogram for the column, so the planner estimates the filtered row count more accurately.

data.title: Interview angle: the planner needs data, not hints
data.text: PostgreSQL has no plan hints, which surprises developers from other databases. The intended workflow is to give the planner better information — accurate statistics, correct cost constants such as `random_page_cost` on SSDs, and indexes that match the predicates — rather than to force a plan. When asked why a query changed plan overnight, the honest first answer is usually that the data distribution or row counts changed and the statistics now tell a different story.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: The query planner chooses execution paths based on estimated I/O and CPU cost.
On SSDs, set `random_page_cost` to 1.1 - 1.2 to enable faster index paths.
Ensure `ANALYZE` runs regularly to maintain accurate planner statistics.
